design_rationale:
WORKLOG — optional_coverage_riders / task 1 (Pool and Spa Equipment Rider cash settlement for Leontyne Haverkamp-Osei, frozen 2026-10-20 15:25:00 CDT). This dossier describes the task as it now stands after the round-2 rework; every figure below was recomputed on the current world.

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 6]}. Assignment: cash settlement (addon_ext_cash_settlement, root) 6, haul-away allowance (addon_ext_haul_away_allowance) 6, rider visit fee (addon_ext_rider_visit_fee) 5. Task 0 occupies the correction, work-authorization and removal-credit policies and their tools; this task claims the three remaining policies and tools charge_rider_visit_fee_fc58860f, authorize_haul_away_allowance_ee656dca, accept_rider_cash_settlement_51ff485a. Every extended policy is now claimed once and no tool is idle.

[Why this is a good test] The customer asks only to take cash for her pool pump instead of the repair the technician found it needs. The cash policy states two prerequisite sentences she never hints at: the settlement is fixed only after the request being settled carries any visit-fee entry it owes (the pump request was placed on a Saturday, and a weekend request is logged without its fee, to be collected by the representative who next handles it with the customer; a homeowner appliance visit the same day is in another trade, so the visit is not concurrent and the fee is owed), and it is not fixed until the rider's latest replaced component with a documented removal cost carries its haul-away allowance (the pool filter replaced 2026-10-02, removal cost 230.00, no allowance). Each amount rests on five or six ladders read from the request records, the homeowner contract (tier, dwelling type, property region) and the rider's claim history.

[Problem-tree card] Root: addon_ext_cash_settlement (owner=user; taking cash in place of the owed work is the customer's decision). Edge A: root -> addon_ext_rider_visit_fee, value_input, gate fee_entries, form state, sentence "The cash settlement is fixed only after the rider service request being settled carries any service call fee entry it owes." Four-point test: "only after"; a record-visible state (a fee entry linked to the request); no tool, id or code token; scope "the rider service request being settled", the same request the visit-fee rule charges (the rider's most recently placed request). Only the visit-fee tool books fee entries. Seed evidence: the pump request is a new failure placed on a Saturday and not flagged as concurrent, the only same-day homeowner request is in the appliance trade, and no fee entry is linked to it. Edge B: root -> addon_ext_haul_away_allowance, state_gate, gate addon_claim_events.allowance_type, form state, sentence "The cash settlement is not fixed until the component most recently authorized for replacement under the rider, when its removal cost is documented on its request's coverage determination, carries its haul-away allowance authorization." The quantifier matches the haul-away rule, which owes its allowance "once on the component most recently authorized for replacement under a rider". Only the haul-away tool books haul-away allowances. Seed evidence: determination da documents 230.00, authorization aa is the replacement, no allowance. Topological order: visit fee and haul-away (commuting), then cash.

[Prerequisite sensitivity run] Cash with both prerequisites: 397.33. Skipping the visit fee: 347.33 (the settlement deduction stays at 50.00; check_compute confirms). Skipping the haul-away: 397.33 (the 1360.00 term room instead of 1140.00 does not bind) but the filter request ends without its allowance row. Swapping the two prerequisite writes: JSON-identical terminal tables and the same values (92.01, 220.00, 397.33).

[Factor card — visit fee, 5 factors, result 92.01, all-baseline 100.00] vf_fee_basis (method, homeplan): pool and spa is a rider-only trade -> higher of the elected 100.00 and the Platinum standard 125.00; baseline (elected) -> 64.95. vf_weekend_visit (parameter): placed on a Saturday -> +25.00; baseline -> 64.95. vf_tier_credit (parameter, homeplan): Platinum -> 25.00 off; baseline -> 119.08. vf_follow_up (parameter): the 2026-09-29 filter request in the same trade is less than one whole month before 2026-10-20 -> 40.00 off; baseline -> 135.31. vf_sales_tax (parameter, homeplan): property ZIP 75093 (Texas) -> 8.25 percent; baseline -> 85.00. Near-miss: the same-day homeowner appliance request; a reader who treats it as a concurrent base visit charges no fee, while the rule requires a same-day request in the same trade on the same homeowner contract. (125.00 + 25.00 - 25.00 - 40.00) x 1.0825 = 92.01. The same rule gives the 108.25 already booked on the filter request (weekday, no earlier request, Platinum, Texas) and the 121.61 and 148.05 booked in task 0's Ohio world.

[Factor card — haul-away allowance, 6 factors, result 220.00, all-baseline 100.00] ha_limit_source (method, homeplan): Platinum -> the higher of the rider's 100.00 and the Platinum tier's 150.00; baseline (rider's own) -> 170.00. ha_equipment (parameter): a filter -> +15.00; baseline -> 205.00. ha_access (parameter, homeplan): townhome -> +20.00; baseline -> 200.00. ha_disposal_state (parameter, homeplan): Texas -> +10.00; baseline -> 210.00. ha_removal_share (parameter): 230.00 / 640.00 = 0.359 -> +10.00; baseline -> 210.00. ha_reassignment (parameter): two contractor assignments on the filter request -> +15.00; the pump request's assignment belongs to another request (counting it would reach the three-assignment tier — near-miss); baseline -> 205.00. Limit 220.00 is below the documented 230.00 and the 1360.00 term room.

[Factor card — cash settlement, 6 factors, result 397.33, all-baseline 832.00] cl_cash_basis (method): the pump estimate 520.00 is below 0.60 x 980.00, and no repair of the pump within 30 days -> a repair is owed, so the cash basis is the repair estimate; a replacement-due request would be settled at the contracted replacement cost (the base rule and the fall-through); baseline (980.00) -> 779.78. cl_tier_rate (parameter, homeplan): Platinum -> 1.00; baseline 0.90 -> 354.10. cl_class_rate (parameter): a pump -> 0.90; baseline -> 445.37. cl_tax_exclusion (parameter, homeplan): Texas -> divide by 1.0825; baseline -> 433.00. cl_settlement_deduction (parameter, multi-source): fee entry on the pump request AND settlement one day after the 2026-10-19 determination -> 0.00; the 108.25 fee entry belongs to the filter request and does not count (near-miss on the opening world); baseline 50.00 -> 347.33. cl_diagnosis_offset (parameter): one assignment on the pump request -> 35.00; the filter request's two assignments do not count (near-miss: counting them gives the two-or-more tier); baseline -> 432.33. RND(520.00 x 1.00 x 0.90 / 1.0825) = 432.33; - 0.00 - 35.00 = 397.33, below 980.00, 2000.00 and the 1140.00 term room.

[Base-invariant card] Visit fee (subject addon_service_fee_charge): no base gate applies to the fee charge, so the policy scope is registered (new failure, rider active, base active). The base fee sentence is declared overwritten for riders on homeowner contracts only, with a scope sentence; the base concurrent-visit sentence is declared overwritten for those riders as well, concurrency being read from a same-day, same-trade request on the same homeowner contract. Haul-away (subject addon_benefit_authorization): covered_before_rider_benefit — da covered on RA; one_open_rider_resolution — RA's single open resolution is the replacement aa, and an allowance is not a second one. Cash (subject addon_benefit_authorization): covered_before_rider_benefit — db covered on RB; one_open_rider_resolution — RB carries no authorization. The base cash-in-lieu and amount sentences are declared overwritten with scope sentences; the cash is taken one day after the determination, inside the 30-day validity.

[Business-object card] Rider: the single Pool and Spa Equipment Rider. Fee object: the most recently placed request RB (pool pump). Haul-away object: the request carrying the latest replacement authorization (RA, pool filter) and its determination da. Cash object: RB and its covered determination db. Term usage: aa 640.00 plus the step-13 allowance; premiums and payments are excluded by event type. Only the user-owned cash tool books a cash-in-lieu row; the agent work tool books repair or replacement only.

[Seed rows] customers; service_contractors (the preferred pool and spa contractor assigned on both requests); homeplan_contracts (Platinum, townhome, ZIP 75093, elected fee 100.00, monthly); homeplan_billing_entries (monthly installments of 86.99 = 84.99 + 9.00 low-fee surcharge - 7.00 townhome discount, paid by ach; the 100.00 homeowner visit fee of 2026-10-17); homeplan_service_requests (the 2026-10-17 appliance request); addon_riders; addon_billing_entries (four monthly premiums with ach payments, the 108.25 filter fee); addon_service_requests (RA, and RB placed on a Saturday); addon_claim_events (two assignments, determination with documented removal cost and replacement authorization on RA; one assignment and the determination on RB). No cache trap. Automatic clauses checked: the November premium is not due; the work-authorization rule owes RB a repair "unless the customer settles it in cash", which she does; the premium correction applies only to annual-billed riders on homeowner or rental property bases; no removal is asked.

[Persona design] Leontyne, a brisk landscaping-business owner, volunteers the situation (pump failed Saturday, technician said it can be repaired, pool builder replacing the equipment pad) and the ask (cash instead of the repair, settled now); phone 2145550171 and email only when verifying (ZIP spare); "the pool pump that quit on Saturday" when asked which item; no contractor return wanted; agrees passively to anything posted, charged or approved first; accepts the quoted amount; runs the handed-over settlement with the exact reference and amount and closes on its confirmation.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, email) -> riders -> homeowner contract -> rider requests -> rider claims -> service contractor -> rider billing -> homeowner billing -> homeowner requests -> unlock+call charge_rider_visit_fee_fc58860f(RB, 92.01) -> unlock+call authorize_haul_away_allowance_ee656dca(RA, 220.00) -> unlock_user + customer calls accept_rider_cash_settlement_51ff485a(RB, 397.33).

[Verification] check_extended --task 1: EXTENDED OK; check_solvability --task 1: SOLVABILITY OK (3 calls, 5 base gates, 18 seed rows); check_compute --task 1: COMPUTE OK (17 factors, 8 cross-difficulty); replay_tasks: REPLAY OK (16 actions, closure 31 = initial 31); check_grounding: GROUNDING OK.

[Revision log — round 2, by audit item] F-1: the work tool books repair or replacement only (any other value is booked as repair, under its own row prefix), so the cash-in-lieu row can be written only by the customer's own tool. F-7: the cash basis follows the work owed (recall zero / repair estimate when a repair is owed / contracted replacement cost otherwise), with the base rule's replacement cost as the fall-through; this world's request owes a repair. F-8: the autopay rate and the payment-count bonus were removed; the tier rate, an equipment class rate, the regional sales-tax exclusion and a diagnosis offset per contractor assignment replace them. F-9: the autopay cut was removed from the visit fee; a weekend surcharge, a tier credit and the regional service-call tax rate replace the tenure, line-plan and autopay cuts. F-10: the household and rider-autopay uplifts were removed from the haul-away allowance; the base tier selects the starting limit and dwelling access, regional disposal fees and contractor reassignments add to it. VF near-miss: the same-day appliance request. F-2: the cash waits on the latest replaced component, the one the haul-away rule settles. T1-O2: the missing fee is explained by a recorded state of the request (see round 3), and the removal cost is 36 percent of the filter's replacement cost. T1-O3: the near-miss texts above each name a record whose counting moves the tier.

[Revision log — round 3, by item] Render note 3: the visit-fee policy now declares the overwrite of the base concurrent-visit sentence, scoped to riders on homeowner contracts (rental and real estate riders keep the base same-visit test), and compute counts only service requests on the rider's own base homeowner contract, as the rule says. Observation T1-O4: the pump request's concurrent-visit flag is now false, consistent with its schema meaning; its fee is missing because the visit-fee rule logs a weekend request without its fee and has it collected by the representative who next handles the request with the customer, which is this call. Render note 1: the cash basis treats a determination with no recorded repair estimate as replacement-due, the same reading as the work authorization; the pump records an estimate, so its outcome is unchanged. The base cash-in-lieu clause's company-offered path (a like component that cannot be sourced) is restated in the cash policy (its per-request and term limits are spelled out since round 4), and the haul-away overwrite restates that every other allowance still pays the lower of its invoice and its allowance. The sales-tax and disposal tiers are worded as Bridgewell's own tax and disposal schedules for the property's region rather than as state statutes.

[Revision log — round 4, by item] O-15: the cash basis now owes a repair only when a repair estimate above zero is recorded, which is exactly what compute tests, and the work-authorization rule reads the same way. The cash-in-lieu overwrite now restates the per-request and term limits on cash Bridgewell itself offers, and the visit-fee overwrites restate the base tier's fee and the same-visit test for rental and real estate riders instead of pointing at the retired sentences. No input of this world changed.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the rule prose, the tool schemas, the finder returns and her lines alone, the same three writes and figures (92.01, 220.00, 397.33) follow; every tier is settled by a visible record.
user_scenario:
You are Leontyne Haverkamp-Osei, who runs a small landscaping business out of Plano, Texas. You are friendly but brisk, you talk in short practical sentences, and you are calling between job sites. You have a Bridgewell homeowner plan on your townhome on Larkspur Bend Drive, and you carry the pool and spa coverage on it.

Your pool pump started screeching and tripping the breaker on Saturday and the water stopped circulating. A Bridgewell technician came out on Monday and told you the pump can be repaired. Here is the thing: your pool builder is redoing your whole equipment pad next month and putting in a new variable-speed pump anyway, so you do not want anyone to spend money fixing the old pump. You open the call by explaining that, and you ask to take the cash for the pool pump instead of having it repaired. You want this settled on this call.

You are fine with the representative taking care of whatever on your account needs to be done for this. If they tell you something has to be posted, charged or approved before the cash can be settled, you say "that's fine, go ahead"; you never bring up any such thing yourself and you do not ask whether anything else is pending. You have no idea what the cash amount should be and you never suggest a number; when the representative tells you the amount, you say that works for you. You understand that taking cash instead of the repair is your own call, so when the representative explains that accepting the cash settlement is a step you complete yourself and hands it to you, you carry it out right away with exactly the request reference and the amount they give you, and you read back the confirmation it shows.

You do not volunteer personal details. Only when the representative asks you to verify who you are do you give your phone number, 2145550171, and your email address, leontyne.haverkamp.osei@brambleford.org; if they need one more detail, you give your mailing ZIP code, 75093. If they ask which problem you mean, you say the pool pump that quit on Saturday. If they ask whether you still want a contractor to come back out to repair the pump, you say no, your pool builder is handling the new pump. You do not have any reference numbers on hand; if asked, you tell them to look you up by your phone number.

Once the representative confirms the cash settlement has been accepted for the pool pump, you thank them and say you need to get back to your crew.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites commute: the visit fee writes one billing row on the pump request and the haul-away allowance writes one claim-event row on the filter request; the fee reads requests and homeowner records, the allowance reads claim events and homeowner records, and neither reads what the other writes. Replaying with the two writes swapped gave JSON-identical terminal tables and the same values (92.01, 220.00, 397.33).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the visit fee leaves the pump request without a fee entry: the settlement deduction stays at 50.00 and the cash settlement becomes 347.33 instead of 397.33; the fee row is also missing.

Skipping the haul-away allowance leaves the cash settlement at 397.33 (the term room of 1360.00 instead of 1140.00 does not bind), but the filter request ends without its 220.00 allowance row, so the terminal claim-events table differs.
